evidence:
I checked every criterion that uses 'every/all/each/only/none/exactly one' and every 'unchanged/nothing changes' guard.

PLURAL ASKS THAT ARE GRADED OVER THE WHOLE COLLECTION (good): hro_bulk_all_or_none says 'none of the set moves' and fails 'if any card of a refused set moves by either route'. hro_bulk_places says 'none moves'. hro_undo_conflict fails 'if the undo goes ahead or partly applies'. hro_undo_restores names every card and the full Applied order 'Y, W, X, Z, A2'. hro_thread_earlier says 'until none remain' and fails on 'missing, repeated, out of order'. hro_candidate_private says 'no response a candidate page receives contains', backed by protocol K: 'Capture every request the candidate page makes and inspect every response'. hro_activity requires a line for 'every successful action you performed on J1 and J2 ... each card of every single and multi-card move ... every undo', and says filtering 'shows all of that job's lines and only those'. hro_activity_refusals says 'none of the refused attempts in this review added a line'. The constraints gate asks for 'exactly one card for that candidate in Applied' in the independent context. hro_unread_counts fails 'if any count is wrong, shared between people'. hro_restart covers 'your jobs, card order per stage, notes, messages and activity lines'.

UNCHANGED GUARDS THAT ALLOW LEGITIMATE SIDE EFFECTS (good): The prompt guard (functional/prompt.md:19) is limited to domain data: 'A refused action must not change any card, order, message or note'. Read markers, sessions and drafts are left out, so the Observer opening a conversation is not punished. hro_thread_access tests the Observer's send as 'refused with nothing added', not 'nothing changes'. hro_seen tests that 'after only the Observer opens' the message is 'still not seen'. This matches rules section 6 'Seen'. In hro_undo_restores and protocol B(12), the note added to A2 is explicitly tolerated: 'a note is not a change', which matches rules line 99. In L and B(10-11), the other person's intervening move happens before the refused undo, so the 'nothing changes' readback is relative to that legitimate move. Activity lines from refusals are deducted only in hro_activity_refusals (prompt:19, 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row'). Earlier reviews' records are tolerated ('never rely on starting counts', app_context.md:30-31), and hro_restart only forbids reloading the starting data. test.sh run_suite uses --max-concurrent-agent 1, so Polish's Noor message and Mei move cannot disturb Functional's 'total by two' or 'does not raise his count or total' readings.

NOTE-LEVEL INSTANCES (P3, no counterexample that flips a conforming or broken app, reported for completeness):
(1) hro_activity collection scope differs between criterion and protocol. The criterion says 'every successful action you performed on J1 and J2'. Protocol A (prompt.md:49) says 'every successful action you performed on them in S, M, L, C, B and R'. That leaves out the J2 addition of Tomas's card in T, Rafael's two-stage moves plus reject/reopen of Tomas's card in K, and Mei's move and addition on J1 in V. All of those happen before A. The judge therefore has a wider target (the criterion) and a narrower one (the protocol). Both are still whole-collection checks of every action type, and the rules (section 4) require all of these lines, so a conforming app passes either way. A broken app that logs only some code paths would also be caught by the S/M/B instances.
(2) hro_restart requires 'messages ... unchanged', but protocol D records only 'the last messages of your conversations'. That samples messages, but loss across a restart would show in the last messages, so the risk is negligible.
(3) hro_candidate_view says 'each candidate sees only their own applications', but protocol K signs in only Noor and Tomas. Lena is used only in Z. 'Each' is effectively scoped to the candidates exercised, and K does not forbid signing in as Lena.
(4) polish hro_pol_failed_send requires 'the message text is still in the box and nothing was added to the conversation'. An app could keep the text in the box (as the rules require) and also render a local red 'Not sent - retry' bubble. A judge might read that bubble as 'added to the conversation', although the fail clause targets 'shown as sent'. The golden shows only an error line (threads.js:194), so this is unexercised. It is a latent ambiguity about a legitimate local side effect, not a demonstrated misgrade.

RUNTIME: raw-evidence-index.json states that full configured grading is absent. I re-verified all 6 artifact hashes as matching. No configured judge transcript shows whether the judge actually enumerates every Activity line or every candidate response within budget. This row's wording verdict is static source analysis only.
counterexample: No credible Fail counterexample. Closest latent case: under hro_pol_failed_send, a conforming app keeps the failed text in the box and also shows a local 'Not sent - retry' bubble, and a strict judge reads 'nothing was added to the conversation' as violated.
suggested_fix: Optional: in hro_pol_failed_send, write 'nothing was sent or shown as sent (a local not-sent marker is acceptable)'. In protocol A, write 'in S, M, L, C, B, T, K, R and V' so it matches the criterion's 'every successful action'.
